newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian energy body wants cap on oil pipeline fees.
newsitem.headline: Russian energy body wants cap on oil pipeline fees.

text.p: Russia's Federal Energy Commission plans to cap pipeline transit fees paid by domestic oil producers to transport crude and products, commission chairman Yuri Korsun said on Wednesday.
Korsun, quoted by Prime-Tass news agency, said that the government agency, set up to introduce more market economy elements into energy exports and tariffs, was seeking to limit producers' costs.

He said his main task was to prevent unjustified growth in pipeline transport fees and related electricity costs which account for 30 percent of transport costs, in order to free up resources at producers and refiners.
The average oil pipeline transit fee in 1997 would fall, he said, because the federal budget had no provision for levying a special pumping fee.
The commission has said it wants to award access to oil pipelines by tender, but the plan has met resistance in the Fuel and Energy Ministry.
Russia's 50,000 km (31,000 mile) crude oil pipeline system is run by state monopoly Transneft and has reservoirs with a capacity of 13.3 million cubic metres.

The entire system is filled at only 50 percent of its total capacity of 500 million tonnes a year (10 million barrels a day) -- but all the export pipelines, with an annual capacity of about 100 million tonnes a year (two million bpd), are full.
Transneft's oil products pipeline system runs 20,500 km (12,700) and has reservoirs of 4.85 million cubic metres.
It has an annual capacity of 60 million tonnes a year (1.2 million bpd) but is filled to only 40 percent of capacity.
